text:
maria: FYI runtime-detector just fired on node gke-prod-12: container 'installer-zz' has a bind mount to /var/run/docker.sock and is running with privileged: true. looks like a hostctl escape attempt? @here

oncall-bot: ALERT: runtime-detector: suspicious-host-socket-bind on gke-prod-12. severity=high. link: https://internal/alerts/32412

sam: Can you paste the pod yaml + ps output from the node?

maria: pod yaml:```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: installer-zz
  namespace: infra-tools
spec:
  containers:
  - name: installer
    image: registry.redwood/internal/installer:sha256-abc123
    securityContext:
      privileged: true
    volumeMounts:
    - mountPath: /var/run/docker.sock
      name: docker-sock
  volumes:
  - name: docker-sock
    hostPath:
      path: /var/run/docker.sock
      type: File
```

maria: node ps snippet:```
root     2345  0.0  0.1  45000  3500 ?        Ssl 10:12   0:00 /usr/bin/containerd
root    23789  0.0  0.0  20000  1500 ?        Ssl 10:15   0:00 /bin/sh -c /tmp/evil.sh
root    23810  0.0  0.0  14000  1200 ?        S    10:15   0:00 /usr/bin/docker -H unix:///var/run/docker.sock ps
```

devinfra: ok cordoning node now and scheduling eviction of non-system pods. running: `kubectl cordon gke-prod-12 && kubectl drain gke-prod-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`

secops: we should snapshot /var/log/kubelet.log, containerd logs, and take a tar of /var/lib/kubelet/pods/<pod-id>/volumes/* and upload to secure-case-324. I also want the containerfs layer id for that image.

natalie: audit logs show a RoleBinding created in infra-tools namespace 19m ago by serviceAccount: infra-agent-sa@infra-tools.rbac:
```
{"timestamp":"2026-03-18T09:56:22Z","actor":"system:serviceaccount:infra-tools:infra-agent-sa","action":"create","resource":"rolebinding","name":"infra-agent-docker-access"}
```

alex: that RoleBinding grants "system:masters"-like cluster-admin perms? looks bad. Can someone pull the RBAC object?

maria: RoleBinding YAML:```
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: infra-agent-docker-access
  namespace: infra-tools
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: infra-agent-sa
  namespace: infra-tools
roleRef:
  kind: ClusterRole
  name: node-admin
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
```

ops-sre: node-admin is a custom clusterrole that allows `patch` on nodes and `create` pods in kube-system. rolling back binding now and removing infra-agent-sa tokens. commands: `kubectl delete rolebinding infra-agent-docker-access -n infra-tools` and `kubectl delete sa infra-agent-sa -n infra-tools`

sam: we should also rotate any KMS encryption keys that the infra-agent could have used — audit shows it called KMS:Encrypt 2 times around the same window. @secops can you trigger KMS key rotation and an access key review?

secops: on it. I revoked the serviceaccount tokens, filed a ticket with cloud KMS team to rotate the key, and started log export for the last 72h to s3://forensics-prod/32412.

devinfra: quick note — do not restart node or kubelet until forensic snapshot completes. we want memory and disk images. I'm attaching the forensic playbook steps.

maria: Communications: I'll ping legal and incident response. initial severity: high, customer impact: none, internal infra impact: potential host compromise. Suggested next: full image scan for registry.redwood/internal/installer:sha256-abc123, check other nodes for similar mounts, and search audit logs for any other RoleBinding creations by infra-agent-sa.

alex: thanks. tagging @oncall to keep the channel live. if anyone sees more hosts with the same pattern, reply here with node name and pod name. :exclamation:

maria: final: collected forensic tar to secure-case-324, node cordoned, pod evicted, RoleBinding deleted, SA removed, KMS rotation requested. moving to incident channel for postmortem.```
